name: caller_turn_mean
definition: arithmetic mean, sum(x)/n of: Complete merged caller segment durations: end − start. Segments still active at the audio boundary are excluded.
rationale: How the caller occupies the floor.
failure: VAD fragmentation, phrase length and task structure may dominate.
missing: At least one observed event; otherwise NaN.

name: caller_turn_median
definition: 50th percentile of: Complete merged caller segment durations: end − start. Segments still active at the audio boundary are excluded.
rationale: How the caller occupies the floor.
failure: VAD fragmentation, phrase length and task structure may dominate.
missing: At least one observed event; otherwise NaN.

name: caller_turn_std
definition: sample standard deviation, sqrt(sum((x−mean)^2)/(n−1)) of: Complete merged caller segment durations: end − start. Segments still active at the audio boundary are excluded.
rationale: How the caller occupies the floor.
failure: VAD fragmentation, phrase length and task structure may dominate.
missing: At least 3 observed comparable events; otherwise NaN.

name: caller_turn_iqr
definition: 75th percentile − 25th percentile, NumPy linear quantiles of: Complete merged caller segment durations: end − start. Segments still active at the audio boundary are excluded.
rationale: How the caller occupies the floor.
failure: VAD fragmentation, phrase length and task structure may dominate.
missing: At least 3 observed comparable events; otherwise NaN.

name: caller_pause_median
definition: 50th percentile of: Gap between consecutive caller segments: next.start − previous.end; may contain agent speech.
rationale: The caller's overall pattern of yielding and returning.
failure: Not a pure thinking-time measure; contains agent turn duration.
missing: At least one observed event; otherwise NaN.

name: response_latency_mean
definition: arithmetic mean, sum(x)/n of: Observed agent-only → optional silence → caller-only handoffs: caller onset − preceding agent offset. Agent continuation and overlap exits are excluded.
rationale: Normal floor-taking timing after the other participant finishes.
failure: A segment boundary is not necessarily the end of a semantic turn.
missing: At least one observed event; otherwise NaN.

name: response_latency_median
definition: 50th percentile of: Observed agent-only → optional silence → caller-only handoffs: caller onset − preceding agent offset. Agent continuation and overlap exits are excluded.
rationale: Normal floor-taking timing after the other participant finishes.
failure: A segment boundary is not necessarily the end of a semantic turn.
missing: At least one observed event; otherwise NaN.

name: interruption_rate
definition: Qualifying agent-onset interruptions / all merged agent segments.
rationale: How frequently the caller was exposed to talk-over.
failure: Agent policy/segmentation is part of this measurement.
missing: No agent segments → NaN. With agent segments but no interruptions, zero is a valid observed rate.

name: interruption_stop_latency_mean
definition: arithmetic mean, sum(x)/n of: For qualifying agent interruptions, caller segment end − agent onset, provided caller end is observed. Includes callers that outlast the agent.
rationale: How long the caller keeps talking after an agent begins over them.
failure: A stop may be natural utterance completion, not caused by the interruption; events are scarce.
missing: At least one observed event; otherwise NaN.

name: interruption_stop_latency_median
definition: 50th percentile of: For qualifying agent interruptions, caller segment end − agent onset, provided caller end is observed. Includes callers that outlast the agent.
rationale: How long the caller keeps talking after an agent begins over them.
failure: A stop may be natural utterance completion, not caused by the interruption; events are scarce.
missing: At least one observed event; otherwise NaN.

name: interruption_yield_fraction
definition: Fraction of interruptions with observed caller end for which caller.end < agent.end − 0.064 s.
example: Caller yields in 2 of 3 resolved interruptions → 0.667.
rationale: Probability of relinquishing the floor during agent talk-over.
failure: Close endpoint ties and early natural utterance endings are ambiguous.
missing: No resolved interruptions → NaN; unresolved outcomes are excluded.

name: interruption_immediate_yield_fraction
definition: Fraction of resolved interruptions with BOTH yielding and caller stop latency ≤0.5 s.
example: 1 of 4 resolved interruptions produces a rapid yield → 0.25.
rationale: Distinguishes prompt yielding from longer continued overlap.
failure: The 0.5 s boundary is a coarse design choice, not an experimentally proven human reflex limit.
missing: No resolved interruptions → NaN.

name: barge_in_rate
definition: Qualifying caller-onset interruptions / all merged caller segments.
example: 2 of 10 caller onsets overlap an already active agent → 0.2.
rationale: How often the caller enters before the agent finishes.
failure: Agent speaking time and VAD boundaries affect the available opportunities.
missing: No caller segments → NaN; zero barge-ins with caller turns is a valid zero rate.

name: barge_overlap_mean
definition: arithmetic mean, sum(x)/n of: For qualifying caller interruptions, min(caller end, agent end) − caller onset. Missing when neither endpoint is observed before the clip boundary.
rationale: Persistence in talk-over and how variable that persistence is.
failure: Padding/crosstalk can create an overlap; timing alone cannot distinguish a backchannel from deliberate interruption.
missing: At least one observed event; otherwise NaN.

name: barge_continues_fraction
definition: Fraction of barge-ins with observed agent end where caller.end > agent.end +0.064 s.
example: Caller outlasts agent in 3 of 4 barge-ins → 0.75.
rationale: Persistence in taking the floor during talk-over.
failure: A short agent segment can make this high without any deliberate persistence.
missing: No barge-ins with observed agent end → NaN.

name: extended_gap_caller_fraction
definition: Fraction of fully observed interior joint silences ≥2 s whose next speaking state is caller-only.
example: Caller ends 3 of 5 long joint gaps → 0.6.
rationale: Who takes the floor after a long gap.
failure: Does not prove that silence was unexpected or intentionally caused by the agent; may encode call flow.
missing: No completed interior long gaps → NaN. Leading/trailing silence excluded.

name: response_latency_std
definition: sample standard deviation, sqrt(sum((x−mean)^2)/(n−1)) of: Observed agent-only → optional silence → caller-only handoffs: caller onset − preceding agent offset. Agent continuation and overlap exits are excluded.
rationale: Normal floor-taking timing after the other participant finishes.
failure: A segment boundary is not necessarily the end of a semantic turn.
missing: At least 3 observed comparable events; otherwise NaN.

name: response_latency_iqr
definition: 75th percentile − 25th percentile, NumPy linear quantiles of: Observed agent-only → optional silence → caller-only handoffs: caller onset − preceding agent offset. Agent continuation and overlap exits are excluded.
rationale: Normal floor-taking timing after the other participant finishes.
failure: A segment boundary is not necessarily the end of a semantic turn.
missing: At least 3 observed comparable events; otherwise NaN.

name: response_latency_cv
definition: sample standard deviation / arithmetic mean of: Observed agent-only → optional silence → caller-only handoffs: caller onset − preceding agent offset. Agent continuation and overlap exits are excluded.
rationale: Normal floor-taking timing after the other participant finishes.
failure: A segment boundary is not necessarily the end of a semantic turn.
missing: At least 3 events, all nonnegative, mean ≥0.1 s; otherwise NaN.

name: barge_overlap_std
definition: sample standard deviation, sqrt(sum((x−mean)^2)/(n−1)) of: For qualifying caller interruptions, min(caller end, agent end) − caller onset. Missing when neither endpoint is observed before the clip boundary.
rationale: Persistence in talk-over and how variable that persistence is.
failure: Padding/crosstalk can create an overlap; timing alone cannot distinguish a backchannel from deliberate interruption.
missing: At least 3 observed comparable events; otherwise NaN.

name: barge_overlap_iqr
definition: 75th percentile − 25th percentile, NumPy linear quantiles of: For qualifying caller interruptions, min(caller end, agent end) − caller onset. Missing when neither endpoint is observed before the clip boundary.
rationale: Persistence in talk-over and how variable that persistence is.
failure: Padding/crosstalk can create an overlap; timing alone cannot distinguish a backchannel from deliberate interruption.
missing: At least 3 observed comparable events; otherwise NaN.

name: barge_overlap_cv
definition: sample standard deviation / arithmetic mean of: For qualifying caller interruptions, min(caller end, agent end) − caller onset. Missing when neither endpoint is observed before the clip boundary.
rationale: Persistence in talk-over and how variable that persistence is.
failure: Padding/crosstalk can create an overlap; timing alone cannot distinguish a backchannel from deliberate interruption.
missing: At least 3 events, all nonnegative, mean ≥0.1 s; otherwise NaN.

name: short_context_response_std
definition: sample standard deviation, sqrt(sum((x−mean)^2)/(n−1)) of: Normal response latencies following a complete agent segment shorter than 3 s.
rationale: Compare variability within a rough, fixed temporal context instead of pooling all events.
failure: Segment length is not a semantic question category; 3 s is a fixed design cutoff.
missing: At least 3 observed comparable events; otherwise NaN.

name: long_context_response_std
definition: sample standard deviation, sqrt(sum((x−mean)^2)/(n−1)) of: Normal response latencies following a complete agent segment at least 3 s long.
rationale: Response variability after longer agent contributions.
failure: Few qualifying events and VAD merging can change context membership.
missing: At least 3 observed comparable events; otherwise NaN.
